title: Eleven Clauses and One Signature
subtitle: 合同与契约 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 合同与契约（社会服务与人际沟通·合同与法律）
meta: 主题语境：合同与契约（社会服务与人际沟通·合同与法律）　|　核心词汇：contract　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 contract 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 my uncle ① signed a contract that ran to eleven clauses, and he said the signing was the whole of the work. The ② contract, meaning the paper and not the job, bound him for a year and stayed binding; contract, he said, is the only thing in a trade that is judged by how little of it is read.

Every ③ contract in that drawer had the same clause nine, and the ④ contract at the end, meaning the one he kept for the big orders and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever argued about twice. Contract, my aunt said, is nine parts clause nine and one part somebody willing to sign; my uncle said the signing is the part that fills the year.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the contract was the whole of the cough, meaning the catching and not the paper. The ⑥ contract, meaning the catching and not any of that, is the only thing in a winter that everybody fears and nobody signs; contract, she said, is either something you sign or the only word that means both a paper and a catching. He said the catching is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ contract had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about clause nine. The ⑧ contract of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in May, was one signature and thirty years of signing; contract, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to read it. She said the reading was never mentioned.

The ⑨ contract I remember is the one at the end, which he signed in 1980 and is still described as the least read in the county. A ⑩ contract, my aunt said in 1982, is the only thing that improves by being argued about; every contract, she said, is a catching that has agreed to look like a paper. She said the catching was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 合同（指那张纸本身，与那份工作相对）
C. 固定搭配：sign a contract 签合同
D. n. 合同（指那个抽屉里每一份）
E. n. 合同（指末尾那一份）
F. v./n. 感染；染上（contract a disease 的用法）
G. n. 合同（指账本里提到的那一份）
H. n. 契约关系（抽象总称）

items.q: signed a contract that ran to eleven clauses
The contract, meaning the paper and not the job
the contract was the whole of the cough
the contract had become a line in a ledger
The contract of the whole thing
A contract, my aunt said in 1982

answers.why: sign a contract 意为“签合同”，1966 年叔叔签了一份长达十一项条款的合同。
contract 意为“合同”，指那张纸本身而不是那份工作，它约束了他一年。
contract 指那个抽屉里每一份合同，每一份的第九条款都一样。
contract 指末尾那一份（他留给大订单的那一份），是唯一有人争论过两次的。
contract 意为“感染、染上”，母亲说染上就是那阵咳嗽的全部，指的是染病而不是那张纸。
contract 为动词义的名词化用法，指染上（疾病）而不是那张纸，是冬天里人人都怕、却无人签字的东西。
contract 意为“合同”，指账本里提到的那一份，到 1974 年这份合同成了账本里的一行。
contract 意为“契约关系”，叔叔五月写道，整件事的契约关系是一个签名三十年的签署。
contract 意为“合同”，我记得的是末尾那一份，他 1980 年签的，至今仍被说成全县最没人读的。
contract 为抽象总称，姑姑说一份合同是唯一会因为被争论而变好的东西。
